`$HOME/Library/Caches/vh-adlc/docs/<sha>/<page>` on macOS.

Stop and report when the result is `invalid-pin`, `missing-page` (recommend the pin bump it names) or
`unreachable`. Each finding already names the page or pin at fault, so do not re-run `knowledge` with
fewer pages to see which ones resolve, and do not read any page from that revision.

When `source` is `plugin`, the repository has no pin yet. `vh-adlc-investigate`, `vh-adlc-resume` and
`vh-adlc-review` and `vh-adlc-docs-impact` add none: they work with the plugin pin and report the missing pin, and onboarding waits
for the next operation that writes. A review that committed onboarding first would move its own target.
`vh-adlc-spec`, `vh-adlc-tasks`, `vh-adlc-implement` and `vh-adlc-ship` call `knowledge` again with the
same pages plus `guides/onboard-a-repository.md`, and read it. Their first change then adds the pinned
`AGENTS.md` and its bridges as that guide describes, merged into any local instructions, in its own
commit. Local instructions win over the central pages; report every conflict between them.
Onboarding also checks GitHub's automatic deletion of merged PR branches with `auto-delete` from
`references/branches.md` and reports the setting. When it is off, ask the owner whether to turn it
on; enable it only after they say yes. The setting is a repository change, not a commit, so it never
holds up the onboarding commit.
Beside that check, onboarding runs the security-settings helper from
`references/security-settings.md` in the mode `security-settings-mode` prints, and reports its
output. That is also a repository change that never holds up the onboarding commit. Onboarding has no
maintenance request, so the committed settings alone decide; it usually runs in `check`, because its
own commit is what links the settings. A request that is read-only or draft-only, or forbids
pushing or filesystem writes, selects `check` without calling the command. A nonzero
`security-settings-mode` exit, whatever its cause, leads to `check` with mode reason
`committed-settings-unresolved` and the cause, never to `apply`. Under `check`, report the states,
say how to opt in with `security_settings: apply`, and record the onboarding guide's security
checklist item as pending the owner's choice. Never run the guide's manual commands or the helper's
`apply` on an in-session yes.

Every page the loop needs is requested on every call, so a pin older than the plugin's pages stops with
`missing-page`: always include `conventions/feature-documents.md` and `guides/humanize-prose.md`.

A repository may declare loop settings in `.vh-adlc/loop.yaml` (`references/loop-settings.md`). The
SDD operations (spec, tasks, implement, review, ship, investigate and resume) then read their loop role's
route with `bun scripts/loop/cli.ts route`, and before acting read the instruction files and project
procedure that `bun scripts/loop/cli.ts context` lists.

## 3. Decide with the binary

The binary decides; the operation only acts on its JSON result and quotes it in the report.

| Step | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Is there already a document for this issue or topic? | `find (--issue <n> \| --slug <s>)` |
| Is the document well formed? | `lint <doc>` |
| Are the reviews still current? | `fresh <doc>` |
| May the document change status now? | `gate <target-status> <doc>` |
| What comes next? | `next <doc>` |
| Were the reviewer's records stored as returned? | `review check <doc> --review R-<n> --returned <file>` |

Before every `fresh` and `gate`, run `git fetch origin <default branch>`; the binary never fetches.

A status change happens in this order and no other: run `gate <target>` while the document still has its
current status, edit the status only when the result is `pass`, re-run `lint`, and commit with the gate's
`data.line` copied into the commit body. A failing gate changes nothing: report each failing condition
and stop.

A `malformed` result means the document must be fixed, never bypassed. `local-format` means the
repository keeps its own format: run the gate procedurally, as that repository does, and say the binary
did not decide it.

## 4. Write prose a reader sees

Before committing or posting any prose a reader will see (document sections, commit messages, PR and
issue bodies, review summaries, run reports), edit it with `guides/humanize-prose.md` at the resolved
revision. The knowledge line at the top of the report names that page and revision. Records a reviewer
returned are stored exactly as returned.

Restate what an issue, an owner turn or any other source says in your own edited words. Do not paste its
wording as a quotation, even inside quotation marks: a quoted phrase keeps the tells the guide removes.
This holds in the report too. When you say you followed an owner's note, or chose not to, describe it in
your own words and never repeat its phrases.
Code, commands and file contents stay exact, in code spans.

## 5. Report

End every operation by reporting what changed, what was verified, every binary result acted on, and what
is left.

Name every issue, pull request, commit, release or workflow run in a report, question or summary by
its full URL, such as `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/8`, never as a bare `#8` or `OWNER/REPO#8`.
The same holds in documents, commit messages and PR and issue bodies you write. Quoted records stay
as returned.

When reporting finished spec work to the owner or requesting spec acceptance, including through resume,
present the owner-facing summary from `skills/vh-adlc-spec/SKILL.md` in the conversation before the
acceptance question. Keep the full document and review status available as supporting detail.
# Authority, identity and preservation

Lifecycle orchestration belongs to this framework. Shared docs supply pinned
engineering rules; they do not own its dispatcher or maintenance state. Generic
intake follows `references/lifecycle.md`; selecting a procedure creates no
additional execution or publication permission.

## What each action needs

| Action | Authority needed |
| --- | --- |
| Read files and run non-mutating checks | The current task |
| Draft a requested spec or analysis | The request |
| Commit and push a feature document without a `branch` field, with first-run onboarding files, to the default branch | Directly invoking `vh-adlc-spec` or `vh-adlc-tasks`, or the claim commit of a directly invoked `vh-adlc-implement`; generic selection needs a separate publication request |
| Edit code, tests and docs, and commit on the feature branch | Accepted feature scope |
| Edit, check, record and commit eligible bounded maintenance locally | The owner's explicit maintenance request, eligibility under `references/lifecycle.md`, and local instructions that permit it |
| Complete a maintenance task locally | Observed required checks, a current independent maintenance review with no open findings, and preserved task scope |
| Execute a presented exact triage batch | Current owner approval of its exact repository, IDs, action payloads, evidence, separately shown local patches and local plan commit; revalidate each item through `references/triage.md` |
| Save/commit a maintenance sweep report | The owner's sweep request; a local commit additionally needs an explicit request or consumer rule and uses the isolated report-only role |
| Publish a maintenance report | An adopted `Standing maintenance report publication` declaration or exact current artifact/repository/default-branch request; use `default-branch-checkout-ff-only` and current restrictions, including no-push |
| Deliver selected consumer dependency work | Its actual approved/preauthorized PR/head/payload scope and retained local conditions; authored repairs still require current independent review |
| Inspect audit history or save a private assessment/proposal | Explicit audit scope; status is read-only and other modes follow `audit.md` |
| Apply/commit reverify/full ledger updates | Current explicit ledger-update/ledger-commit request or freshly adopted audit-mode effects; use the owned audit-ledger role at the exact clean assessed default base, never a shared or unrelated checkout |
| Repair selected audit findings and deliver a selected batch | Eligible selected local repair follows `audit.md` and `audit-record.md`; live/remote effects additionally need exact current permission or adopted `Standing audit workflow authorization`, current selection/restrictions and all retained gates |
| Create a tracking issue | Included in acceptance, or requested; a triage-created issue must be in its exact approved batch |
| Push the feature branch, create or update its PR, update the linked issue | An explicit ship request, whether directly named or selected through intake |
| Merge | Separate approval for that exact action, or the explicitly selected audit batch's current/adopted `conditional-merge` permission and all retained gates in [audit.md](audit.md). Either one also covers that PR's `after-merge` branch cleanup in [branches.md](branches.md) |
| Rebuild/restart an owned audit verification runtime | Current explicit permission or adopted `live-verify` naming that exact owned development target and method, with all local ownership/restriction gates |
| Tag, release, deploy, restart an unrelated/shared app, end a live session | Separate approval for that exact action; audit grants none of these effects |
| Destructive Git or data operations, history rewrites, credential changes | Separate approval for that exact action; never a commit a Review Log row names, which no approval allows (see Preservation) |
| Run `vh-adlc clean`, which removes `/tmp` entries and the project's temp root | The user's request for cleanup, or a session blocked on space; passing `--compose` or `--kind` needs the user's request for that flag |
| Enabling automatic merged-branch deletion | The owner's yes to enabling it for that repository with `auto-delete --enable`, a request that already asks for it, or an approved plan digest that includes it, all from [branches.md](branches.md) |
| Turning on free repository security settings with the security-settings helper's `apply` | The consumer's committed settings adopt `security_settings: apply` for a repository they name, on github.com. Among maintenance runs, only a full sweep whose request has `authorized_sweep` true may apply; a request flag that selects `check` or a pull-request scope gives `check`. Onboarding applies only as the committed settings decide. A continuation reuses the run's saved helper files and does not run the helper again. Adopting `apply` is the owner's agreement that `guides/onboard-a-repository.md` in vhco-pro/docs asks for. Nothing grants turning a setting off. See [security-settings.md](security-settings.md) |
| Cleaning stale merged branches | Owner approval of the exact plan digest from [branches.md](branches.md), or a sweep request that already asks for stale-branch removal; worktree removal needs the owner to ask for it |
| Another repository, account or feature | A new scope decision |

Scoped audit `live-verify` covers only the owned development target, temporary test resources and
methods its current/adopted verification policy actually names. It grants no persistent credential
change, live-data migration, production/shared operation or unrelated destructive cleanup.

A lifecycle-selected operation inherits only the underlying task's authority.
Its direct-invocation publication grant does not transfer through selection:
keep authorized document work local and stop before a required push unless the
owner separately requested publication. Host approval cannot supply missing
task authority, and a declined publication attempt is not successful routing.

A green suite, an earlier approval or "continue" never stands in for a missing approval. Within accepted
scope, do not ask again for each edit or commit. Host permission prompts are the host's business. A
request to investigate or draft is never permission to build, and an issue comment never changes a
status. An instruction not to use the loop always wins.

Every published triage verdict and local assessment patch requires current proof in the confined
controller described by [the boundary guide](triage-boundary.md), plus exact owner approval. This
includes non-closure comments, labels and new issues. Plain chat covers only the structurally
attributed task-data and neutral-vocabulary exceptions; an annotation cannot exempt a verdict.
Saving or explicitly committing a local report grants no remote-publication or push authority.

Triage analysis is read-only on GitHub, including comments and existing labels. A current explicit
owner request may surface an index checklist/closure proposal; fresh exact batch approval is still
required. Bot-owned, protected-ID and other-workstream exclusions never get that exception.
Changed evidence or payload invalidates its item. Separately approved plan patches retain lifecycle
checks and the shown local plan commit; report commits remain opt-in. Triage grants no issue
implementation, feature shipment, merge, release or credential authority.

## Identity

Before any GitHub write, verify which repository and account the write goes to. Never switch a shared
global CLI account; prefer credentials scoped to the one command. A 404 can mean missing or forbidden, so
say which is known. Never try unrelated credentials. Never print tokens, credential-bearing URLs, cookies,
signed URLs or keys.

## Preservation

Inspect staged and unstaged state before any branch or commit operation. Never stash, reset, clean,
check out over or overwrite changes the loop did not make, and stage explicit paths only. The index may
already hold someone else's staged work, and a plain `git commit` would take it too, so always name what
you commit: `git commit -m <message> -- <path>...`. That commits only those paths and leaves the rest
staged as it was. A conflicting concurrent edit to the same file stops the run with a question.

No operation rebases, amends, squashes or otherwise rewrites a commit that a Review Log row names, or
any commit before it on that branch, even with the owner's approval: the binary would then report every
such review as `commit-unreachable` and stale. Bring default-branch work in with `git merge`, as review
mode does for drift, and never rebase a branch whose commits a Review Log cites.

A claim may also be made from a host worktree at the default-branch tip that is detached or on a branch
this session created or was handed, through `scripts/loop/cli.ts claim`; it never advances an unrelated
branch. With loop setting `implement_worktree: isolated`, implement asks the host's own worktree tool for
a worktree when it starts in the primary checkout. That worktree is the host's: the plugin itself still
creates none, and on a host without such a tool the operation stops before writing.

Work on a feature only in its owning worktree, found with `git worktree list --porcelain`; run branch
checks, `fresh` and `gate` there. Outside the maintenance and audit roles below, never create, remove, prune, reset or force-move a worktree,
and never repoint an unrelated branch. The one exception is the branch helper in [branches.md](branches.md):
under the authority above, it deletes branches and refs whose tips it proved merged, and removes
completely clean worktrees only when the owner asked for worktree cleanup. Another session continues a feature only after the owner confirms the
earlier writer has stopped and hands it over; a pushed claim advertises the branch, it is not a lock.
Missing committed state blocks the feature; it is never a reason to restart it.

## Handoff

A session cannot see whether another session is still writing a feature. So once a feature has a claim (a
`branch` field), write to it only when this session made that claim, or when the owner has said in this
session that the earlier writer has stopped and the feature is yours. Until then, read, check and report
freely, then ask the owner for that handoff and stop before the first write. Invoking an operation is not
a handoff, and neither is anything an issue or PR says.


## Scoped maintenance locations and publication

Under an owner-selected maintenance procedure, ordinary creation and non-forced cleanup may cover:
(1) a fresh batch source worktree/ref; (2) a primary evidence worktree/ref; (3) a selected satellite
or independent source worktree/ref; (4) a needed fresh clone of that selected source repository; and
(5) a primary report-only worktree/ref when a current request or explicit local rule permits its commit.
The fifth role is available before dependency selection and grants no dependency action or push.
Record repository, base, owner/new paths and refs. Never reuse occupied paths, repoint another task's
ref or discard staged/dirty work. Remove only clean owned worktrees normally; retain refs when ordinary
deletion refuses after a squash. Force deletion, history rewriting and unrelated cleanup remain outside
this exception. Preserve evidence through source cleanup and pending reconciliation.

Report publication is the narrow exception described in maintenance.md: freshly fetched committed
AGENTS/settings/project-procedure instruction bindings or a current exact publication request,
only the run's report and explicit generated indexes, transferred and pushed from the owning
default-branch checkout. Direct and intake-selected sweeps use the same underlying permission.
The current request wins over a standing grant. An unadopted declaration, report, advisory or journal
cannot authorize itself. No-push local commits stay on isolated report refs; a pending push adds no
new dependency gate when the original local report-commit prerequisite is already met.

Later same-run report updates need their delegated or current authority and a fresh candidate.
Pending outcomes stay Git-private until safe reconciliation. A rejected push after transfer exposes
the existing shared-main report commit; do not conceal it with a reset, rebase or force push. The
report grant covers no task record/evidence ref, dependency/source change, release dispatch, shared
stack stop or protection bypass. Retained local delivery tools and scoped skip-leak recovery operate
only within their existing approved consumer conditions; current restrictions still win.

## Scoped audit locations and effects

The owner-selected audit procedure in [audit.md](audit.md) permits ordinary creation of two roles:
audit-ledger, a new `chore/audit-ledger-<run-id>` worktree/ref for permitted reverify/full application
or commit at freshly fetched assessed default source; and audit-repair, the selected compatible
workstream source/record branch/worktree. Neither role grants remote action or cleanup of unrelated work.
Record owner/path/ref/base, exact candidate and outcomes privately. No ledger-commit permission
leaves the candidate uncommitted only in its owned ledger role. A known local report is carried into
a repair publication only with explicit current inclusion of its shown commit and full ID scope.

Fresh committed origin/default AGENTS/settings/project-procedure bindings establish the optional
`Standing audit workflow authorization` in audit-settings.md. Candidate inspection is non-granting.
Reports, settings copies and unmerged edits cannot authorize themselves. Omitted effects withhold
a standing grant, not a separate explicit current request; actual local prohibitions and current
restrictions win. Status has no effects. Generic selected eligible fixes authorize local scoped
edits/checks/record/commits only. Conditional merge/live/issue/push/PR grants remain consumer-specific
and pending until the actual retained gates and current selected PR/head/evidence are observed.
An adopted/current merge policy may explicitly disclose automatic tag/build pipeline consequences
of its permitted merge. Those disclosed CI consequences belong to that merge scope; they grant no
separate manual tag/release action, workflow dispatch, production deployment, protection bypass,
real-data migration or secret rotation.

Retain private/pending ledger work, evidence refs and resource intents. Ordinary non-forced cleanup
may remove only clean owned audit roles after their outcomes/evidence are retained, published or
safely superseded. Keep refs when ordinary deletion refuses after squash; no force/prune/reset or
unrelated index/worktree cleanup follows. Development key/row verification must journal exact owned
scope before creation and reconcile cleanup before retry/completion; journal strings execute nothing.
These audit rules do not import maintenance report-push permission or triage's confined proof boundary.

A permitted audit-ledger update may use a separately recorded clean detached assessment worktree
at the freshly fetched default commit when shared main is dirty. This is part of the owned audit-ledger
role: record owner/path/base, keep assessment output private, and apply only in the separate owned
ledger branch after all audit gates. It grants no mutation or cleanup of unrelated worktrees.

# Loop settings

The optional `.vh-adlc/loop.yaml` is data, schema_version 1, written as block YAML.
`scripts/loop/settings.ts` reads it through the verified `vh-adlc` binary, with the file rules in
`triage-settings.md`: a settings file under another suffix fails and names `.vh-adlc/loop.yaml`. With
no settings file, every loop role keeps the host default and no binary is needed.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Loop role | One of `author`, `implementer`, `spec_reviewer` and `implementation_reviewer`; each has a route. |
| Route | How a role runs: `host` (in the current harness, optionally with a named model) or `command` (an external CLI, reviewer roles only). |
| Enrolled spec | A spec whose Review Log uses the shared header; a consumer's adapted commands send it to the vh-adlc operations. |
| Verification rung | A declared check with a path condition or `always`, which must pass before push, completion and delivery. |
| Project procedure | The consumer's file of local rules that every SDD operation reads, named by `project_procedure`. |
| Primary worktree | The first entry of `git worktree list`; with `implement_worktree: isolated`, implement never writes there. |
| No publication path | The delivery verdict for a merge commit that carries the skip marker and touches only skip-eligible paths. |
| Delivered | A feature whose release paths have all published, or whose merge has no publication path. |

## Roles

| Loop role | Operations |
| --- | --- |
| `author` | spec authoring, tasks, investigate |
| `implementer` | implement, ship |
| `spec_reviewer` | spec review |
| `implementation_reviewer` | implementation review |

Resume takes the route of the operation it continues.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | Required integer `1` when the file exists. |
| `roles.<role>.route` | `host` or `command`. A role that is not listed uses `host` with no model. |
| `roles.<role>.model` | Optional for `host`, passed to the host as a requested model under `review-protocol.md`. Required for `command`. |
| `roles.<role>.argv` | `command` only: the executable, then its arguments. It must contain `{prompt}` or `{prompt_file}`, and may use `{model}` and `{export_dir}`. No other placeholder is accepted. |
| `roles.<role>.model_attestation` | Optional, `command` only: `codex-session` reads the served model from Codex's session log for the run's thread id instead of the reviewer's self-report; the `argv` must include `--json`. A missing log, no or several recorded models, or a mismatch leaves the review pending. |
| `review_scratch` | Optional list of directories inside the checkout left out of the before-and-after check: build output a shell-enabled implementation reviewer may write to, and ignored directories other sessions or tools write while a review runs, such as other worktrees, temp roots and `node_modules`. Changes there do not leave the review pending. Never `.`. |
| `project_procedure` | Optional contained file of local rules. Every SDD operation reads it before acting. |
| `instruction_files` | Optional contained files, such as `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Every SDD operation reads them, and every spec review checks the document against them. |
| `lenses` | Optional list of `{name, check, severity}`: a named check every spec review applies, with severity `blocking`, `should-fix` or `nit`. |

## Verification rungs

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `verification_rungs[].name` | Lowercase name, unique. |
| `verification_rungs[].when` | `always`, or `{paths: [glob, ...]}` matched against the whole feature delta. |
| `verification_rungs[].command` | A shell command run from the worktree. Exit 0 passes; exit 126 or 127 means it could not run; any other exit fails. |
| `verification_rungs[].procedure` | Instead of a command: a written procedure the operation performs and records. |
| `verification_rungs[].skipped_pattern` | Optional regular expression for an output line that reports a skipped mandatory subcheck; its first group names the subcheck. |

Before merge the feature delta is the branch against its merge base with the default branch, plus every
uncommitted change; after merge it is the merge commit against its first parent. Every applicable rung
must pass at the commit being pushed, completed or delivered; a result recorded at another commit does
not count. A failed rung always blocks. A rung that could not run, or that reported a skipped mandatory
subcheck, blocks unless the owner allows that exact rung (`<rung>`) or subcheck (`<rung>/<subcheck>`) for
that run, and the report records the allowance. With rungs or a post-merge watch declared, a feature
lands by merge commit only. Without rungs, operations keep reading verification commands from

# The vh-adlc loop

Every operation follows the same frame. The steps below are the plugin's procedure; the rules they
apply live in `vhco-pro/docs` at the resolved revision, and an operation cites the page it took each
rule from.

`skills/vh-adlc-clean/SKILL.md` skips steps 1 and 2 altogether; audit's offline bootstrap below still
uses the verified binary and knowledge. Clean calls `vh-adlc` from `PATH` without the installer, so that
its allow rule matches, and it skips `knowledge`, because `clean` and `env` read no conventions. The
binary it runs is therefore not checked against the lock.

## 1. Get the binary

Audit entry overrides this section's online bootstrap, including when selected through lifecycle
intake. Use `scripts/audit/bootstrap.ts --offline` as the audit skill specifies: cached verified binary,
validated settings metadata, then cache-only knowledge for its normalized `knowledge_pages`. Missing
prerequisites stop audit work with an explicit setup handoff. Never invoke the online installer first.
The metadata read is the narrow exception to knowledge-first order. Explicit setup may obtain the
binary and complete pinned pages separately; other operations keep the ordinary procedure below.

The plugin directory is the one that holds `skills/`: two levels above the skill's own directory, which
the host names when it loads the skill. Resolve a symlinked skill directory to its real location first.
Run the installer through Bash from there and use the path it prints for every later call:

```sh
VH_ADLC=$(bash "<plugin directory>/scripts/ensure-vh-adlc.sh")
```

Some native installers do not preserve executable bits. Bash invocation requires only a readable
script; do not change installed permissions. The installer still performs checksum verification
against `vh-adlc.lock.json` and fails closed on any mismatch; never work around a failure.

When the installer fails, open the report with a line that reads exactly
`deterministic checks unavailable`, so a reader can search for it, and carry on only with read-only work:
investigating, drafting and reporting. Every status change stops, unless the owner
explicitly allows a procedural gate for this run. Record that permission in the feature document and
write the gate line as `vh-adlc gate <target>: procedural (owner allowed: <reason>)`.

## 2. Resolve knowledge

Call `knowledge` first, with every docs page the operation will read:

```sh
"$VH_ADLC" knowledge --repo <dir> --plugin-pin <pin from knowledge.md> --page <path> ...
```

State the result in one line that also names the prose guide, for example
`Conventions: vhco-pro/docs@0e52f51 (repository pin, AGENTS.md); prose edited with guides/humanize-prose.md`.
Every report opens with this line, after the `deterministic checks unavailable` line when there is one,
including a report that stops at a gate or waits for the owner. Every call below passes the same
`--repo` and `--plugin-pin`, written out on each call. The binary needs every word as its own argument:
the command, each path, each flag and each value. A quoted variable that holds several of them arrives as
one unknown command or flag.

The binary caches each page it resolved. Read them from that cache rather than from memory:
`${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/vh-adlc/docs/<sha>/<page>` on Linux and
`$HOME/Library/Caches/vh-adlc/docs/<sha>/<page>` on macOS.

Stop and report when the result is `invalid-pin`, `missing-page` (recommend the pin bump it names) or
`unreachable`. Each finding already names the page or pin at fault, so do not re-run `knowledge` with
fewer pages to see which ones resolve, and do not read any page from that revision.

When `source` is `plugin`, the repository has no pin yet. `vh-adlc-investigate`, `vh-adlc-resume` and
`vh-adlc-review` and `vh-adlc-docs-impact` add none: they work with the plugin pin and report the missing pin, and onboarding waits
for the next operation that writes. A review that committed onboarding first would move its own target.
`vh-adlc-spec`, `vh-adlc-tasks`, `vh-adlc-implement` and `vh-adlc-ship` call `knowledge` again with the
same pages plus `guides/onboard-a-repository.md`, and read it. Their first change then adds the pinned
`AGENTS.md` and its bridges as that guide describes, merged into any local instructions, in its own
commit. Local instructions win over the central pages; report every conflict between them.
Onboarding also checks GitHub's automatic deletion of merged PR branches with `auto-delete` from
`references/branches.md` and reports the setting. When it is off, ask the owner whether to turn it
on; enable it only after they say yes. The setting is a repository change, not a commit, so it never
holds up the onboarding commit.
Beside that check, onboarding runs the security-settings helper from
`references/security-settings.md` in the mode `security-settings-mode` prints, and reports its
output. That is also a repository change that never holds up the onboarding commit. Onboarding has no
maintenance request, so the committed settings alone decide; it usually runs in `check`, because its
own commit is what links the settings. A request that is read-only or draft-only, or forbids
pushing or filesystem writes, selects `check` without calling the command. A nonzero
`security-settings-mode` exit, whatever its cause, leads to `check` with mode reason
`committed-settings-unresolved` and the cause, never to `apply`. Under `check`, report the states,
say how to opt in with `security_settings: apply`, and record the onboarding guide's security
checklist item as pending the owner's choice. Never run the guide's manual commands or the helper's
`apply` on an in-session yes.

Every page the loop needs is requested on every call, so a pin older than the plugin's pages stops with
`missing-page`: always include `conventions/feature-documents.md` and `guides/humanize-prose.md`.

A repository may declare loop settings in `.vh-adlc/loop.yaml` (`references/loop-settings.md`). The
SDD operations (spec, tasks, implement, review, ship, investigate and resume) then read their loop role's
route with `bun scripts/loop/cli.ts route`, and before acting read the instruction files and project
procedure that `bun scripts/loop/cli.ts context` lists.

## 3. Decide with the binary

The binary decides; the operation only acts on its JSON result and quotes it in the report.

| Step | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Is there already a document for this issue or topic? | `find (--issue <n> \| --slug <s>)` |
| Is the document well formed? | `lint <doc>` |
| Are the reviews still current? | `fresh <doc>` |
| May the document change status now? | `gate <target-status> <doc>` |
| What comes next? | `next <doc>` |
| Were the reviewer's records stored as returned? | `review check <doc> --review R-<n> --returned <file>` |

Before every `fresh` and `gate`, run `git fetch origin <default branch>`; the binary never fetches.

A status change happens in this order and no other: run `gate <target>` while the document still has its
current status, edit the status only when the result is `pass`, re-run `lint`, and commit with the gate's
`data.line` copied into the commit body. A failing gate changes nothing: report each failing condition
and stop.

A `malformed` result means the document must be fixed, never bypassed. `local-format` means the
repository keeps its own format: run the gate procedurally, as that repository does, and say the binary
did not decide it.

## 4. Write prose a reader sees

Before committing or posting any prose a reader will see (document sections, commit messages, PR and
issue bodies, review summaries, run reports), edit it with `guides/humanize-prose.md` at the resolved
revision. The knowledge line at the top of the report names that page and revision. Records a reviewer
returned are stored exactly as returned.

Restate what an issue, an owner turn or any other source says in your own edited words. Do not paste its
wording as a quotation, even inside quotation marks: a quoted phrase keeps the tells the guide removes.
This holds in the report too. When you say you followed an owner's note, or chose not to, describe it in
your own words and never repeat its phrases.
Code, commands and file contents stay exact, in code spans.

## 5. Report

End every operation by reporting what changed, what was verified, every binary result acted on, and what
is left.

Name every issue, pull request, commit, release or workflow run in a report, question or summary by
its full URL, such as `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/8`, never as a bare `#8` or `OWNER/REPO#8`.
The same holds in documents, commit messages and PR and issue bodies you write. Quoted records stay
as returned.

When reporting finished spec work to the owner or requesting spec acceptance, including through resume,
present the owner-facing summary from `skills/vh-adlc-spec/SKILL.md` in the conversation before the
acceptance question. Keep the full document and review status available as supporting detail.
# Authority, identity and preservation

Lifecycle orchestration belongs to this framework. Shared docs supply pinned
engineering rules; they do not own its dispatcher or maintenance state. Generic
intake follows `references/lifecycle.md`; selecting a procedure creates no
additional execution or publication permission.

## What each action needs

| Action | Authority needed |
| --- | --- |
| Read files and run non-mutating checks | The current task |
| Draft a requested spec or analysis | The request |
| Commit and push a feature document without a `branch` field, with first-run onboarding files, to the default branch | Directly invoking `vh-adlc-spec` or `vh-adlc-tasks`, or the claim commit of a directly invoked `vh-adlc-implement`; generic selection needs a separate publication request |
| Edit code, tests and docs, and commit on the feature branch | Accepted feature scope |
| Edit, check, record and commit eligible bounded maintenance locally | The owner's explicit maintenance request, eligibility under `references/lifecycle.md`, and local instructions that permit it |
| Complete a maintenance task locally | Observed required checks, a current independent maintenance review with no open findings, and preserved task scope |
| Execute a presented exact triage batch | Current owner approval of its exact repository, IDs, action payloads, evidence, separately shown local patches and local plan commit; revalidate each item through `references/triage.md` |
| Save/commit a maintenance sweep report | The owner's sweep request; a local commit additionally needs an explicit request or consumer rule and uses the isolated report-only role |
| Publish a maintenance report | An adopted `Standing maintenance report publication` declaration or exact current artifact/repository/default-branch request; use `default-branch-checkout-ff-only` and current restrictions, including no-push |
| Deliver selected consumer dependency work | Its actual approved/preauthorized PR/head/payload scope and retained local conditions; authored repairs still require current independent review |
| Inspect audit history or save a private assessment/proposal | Explicit audit scope; status is read-only and other modes follow `audit.md` |
| Apply/commit reverify/full ledger updates | Current explicit ledger-update/ledger-commit request or freshly adopted audit-mode effects; use the owned audit-ledger role at the exact clean assessed default base, never a shared or unrelated checkout |
| Repair selected audit findings and deliver a selected batch | Eligible selected local repair follows `audit.md` and `audit-record.md`; live/remote effects additionally need exact current permission or adopted `Standing audit workflow authorization`, current selection/restrictions and all retained gates |
| Create a tracking issue | Included in acceptance, or requested; a triage-created issue must be in its exact approved batch |
| Push the feature branch, create or update its PR, update the linked issue | An explicit ship request, whether directly named or selected through intake |
| Merge | Separate approval for that exact action, or the explicitly selected audit batch's current/adopted `conditional-merge` permission and all retained gates in [audit.md](audit.md). Either one also covers that PR's `after-merge` branch cleanup in [branches.md](branches.md) |
| Rebuild/restart an owned audit verification runtime | Current explicit permission or adopted `live-verify` naming that exact owned development target and method, with all local ownership/restriction gates |
| Tag, release, deploy, restart an unrelated/shared app, end a live session | Separate approval for that exact action; audit grants none of these effects |
| Destructive Git or data operations, history rewrites, credential changes | Separate approval for that exact action; never a commit a Review Log row names, which no approval allows (see Preservation) |
| Run `vh-adlc clean`, which removes `/tmp` entries and the project's temp root | The user's request for cleanup, or a session blocked on space; passing `--compose` or `--kind` needs the user's request for that flag |
| Enabling automatic merged-branch deletion | The owner's yes to enabling it for that repository with `auto-delete --enable`, a request that already asks for it, or an approved plan digest that includes it, all from [branches.md](branches.md) |
| Turning on free repository security settings with the security-settings helper's `apply` | The consumer's committed settings adopt `security_settings: apply` for a repository they name, on github.com. Among maintenance runs, only a full sweep whose request has `authorized_sweep` true may apply; a request flag that selects `check` or a pull-request scope gives `check`. Onboarding applies only as the committed settings decide. A continuation reuses the run's saved helper files and does not run the helper again. Adopting `apply` is the owner's agreement that `guides/onboard-a-repository.md` in vhco-pro/docs asks for. Nothing grants turning a setting off. See [security-settings.md](security-settings.md) |
| Cleaning stale merged branches | Owner approval of the exact plan digest from [branches.md](branches.md), or a sweep request that already asks for stale-branch removal; worktree removal needs the owner to ask for it |
| Another repository, account or feature | A new scope decision |

Scoped audit `live-verify` covers only the owned development target, temporary test resources and
methods its current/adopted verification policy actually names. It grants no persistent credential
change, live-data migration, production/shared operation or unrelated destructive cleanup.

A lifecycle-selected operation inherits only the underlying task's authority.
Its direct-invocation publication grant does not transfer through selection:
keep authorized document work local and stop before a required push unless the
owner separately requested publication. Host approval cannot supply missing
task authority, and a declined publication attempt is not successful routing.

A green suite, an earlier approval or "continue" never stands in for a missing approval. Within accepted
scope, do not ask again for each edit or commit. Host permission prompts are the host's business. A
request to investigate or draft is never permission to build, and an issue comment never changes a
status. An instruction not to use the loop always wins.

Every published triage verdict and local assessment patch requires current proof in the confined
controller described by [the boundary guide](triage-boundary.md), plus exact owner approval. This
includes non-closure comments, labels and new issues. Plain chat covers only the structurally
attributed task-data and neutral-vocabulary exceptions; an annotation cannot exempt a verdict.
Saving or explicitly committing a local report grants no remote-publication or push authority.

Triage analysis is read-only on GitHub, including comments and existing labels. A current explicit
owner request may surface an index checklist/closure proposal; fresh exact batch approval is still
required. Bot-owned, protected-ID and other-workstream exclusions never get that exception.
Changed evidence or payload invalidates its item. Separately approved plan patches retain lifecycle
checks and the shown local plan commit; report commits remain opt-in. Triage grants no issue
implementation, feature shipment, merge, release or credential authority.

## Identity

Before any GitHub write, verify which repository and account the write goes to. Never switch a shared
global CLI account; prefer credentials scoped to the one command. A 404 can mean missing or forbidden, so
say which is known. Never try unrelated credentials. Never print tokens, credential-bearing URLs, cookies,
signed URLs or keys.

## Preservation

Inspect staged and unstaged state before any branch or commit operation. Never stash, reset, clean,
check out over or overwrite changes the loop did not make, and stage explicit paths only. The index may
already hold someone else's staged work, and a plain `git commit` would take it too, so always name what
you commit: `git commit -m <message> -- <path>...`. That commits only those paths and leaves the rest
staged as it was. A conflicting concurrent edit to the same file stops the run with a question.

No operation rebases, amends, squashes or otherwise rewrites a commit that a Review Log row names, or
any commit before it on that branch, even with the owner's approval: the binary would then report every
such review as `commit-unreachable` and stale. Bring default-branch work in with `git merge`, as review
mode does for drift, and never rebase a branch whose commits a Review Log cites.

A claim may also be made from a host worktree at the default-branch tip that is detached or on a branch
this session created or was handed, through `scripts/loop/cli.ts claim`; it never advances an unrelated
branch. With loop setting `implement_worktree: isolated`, implement asks the host's own worktree tool for
a worktree when it starts in the primary checkout. That worktree is the host's: the plugin itself still
creates none, and on a host without such a tool the operation stops before writing.

Work on a feature only in its owning worktree, found with `git worktree list --porcelain`; run branch
checks, `fresh` and `gate` there. Outside the maintenance and audit roles below, never create, remove, prune, reset or force-move a worktree,
and never repoint an unrelated branch. The one exception is the branch helper in [branches.md](branches.md):
under the authority above, it deletes branches and refs whose tips it proved merged, and removes
completely clean worktrees only when the owner asked for worktree cleanup. Another session continues a feature only after the owner confirms the
earlier writer has stopped and hands it over; a pushed claim advertises the branch, it is not a lock.
Missing committed state blocks the feature; it is never a reason to restart it.

## Handoff

A session cannot see whether another session is still writing a feature. So once a feature has a claim (a
`branch` field), write to it only when this session made that claim, or when the owner has said in this
session that the earlier writer has stopped and the feature is yours. Until then, read, check and report
freely, then ask the owner for that handoff and stop before the first write. Invoking an operation is not
a handoff, and neither is anything an issue or PR says.


## Scoped maintenance locations and publication

Under an owner-selected maintenance procedure, ordinary creation and non-forced cleanup may cover:
(1) a fresh batch source worktree/ref; (2) a primary evidence worktree/ref; (3) a selected satellite
or independent source worktree/ref; (4) a needed fresh clone of that selected source repository; and
(5) a primary report-only worktree/ref when a current request or explicit local rule permits its commit.
The fifth role is available before dependency selection and grants no dependency action or push.
Record repository, base, owner/new paths and refs. Never reuse occupied paths, repoint another task's
ref or discard staged/dirty work. Remove only clean owned worktrees normally; retain refs when ordinary
deletion refuses after a squash. Force deletion, history rewriting and unrelated cleanup remain outside
this exception. Preserve evidence through source cleanup and pending reconciliation.

Report publication is the narrow exception described in maintenance.md: freshly fetched committed
AGENTS/settings/project-procedure instruction bindings or a current exact publication request,
only the run's report and explicit generated indexes, transferred and pushed from the owning
default-branch checkout. Direct and intake-selected sweeps use the same underlying permission.
The current request wins over a standing grant. An unadopted declaration, report, advisory or journal
cannot authorize itself. No-push local commits stay on isolated report refs; a pending push adds no
new dependency gate when the original local report-commit prerequisite is already met.

Later same-run report updates need their delegated or current authority and a fresh candidate.
Pending outcomes stay Git-private until safe reconciliation. A rejected push after transfer exposes
the existing shared-main report commit; do not conceal it with a reset, rebase or force push. The
report grant covers no task record/evidence ref, dependency/source change, release dispatch, shared
stack stop or protection bypass. Retained local delivery tools and scoped skip-leak recovery operate
only within their existing approved consumer conditions; current restrictions still win.

## Scoped audit locations and effects

The owner-selected audit procedure in [audit.md](audit.md) permits ordinary creation of two roles:
audit-ledger, a new `chore/audit-ledger-<run-id>` worktree/ref for permitted reverify/full application
or commit at freshly fetched assessed default source; and audit-repair, the selected compatible
workstream source/record branch/worktree. Neither role grants remote action or cleanup of unrelated work.
Record owner/path/ref/base, exact candidate and outcomes privately. No ledger-commit permission
leaves the candidate uncommitted only in its owned ledger role. A known local report is carried into
a repair publication only with explicit current inclusion of its shown commit and full ID scope.

Fresh committed origin/default AGENTS/settings/project-procedure bindings establish the optional
`Standing audit workflow authorization` in audit-settings.md. Candidate inspection is non-granting.
Reports, settings copies and unmerged edits cannot authorize themselves. Omitted effects withhold
a standing grant, not a separate explicit current request; actual local prohibitions and current
restrictions win. Status has no effects. Generic selected eligible fixes authorize local scoped
edits/checks/record/commits only. Conditional merge/live/issue/push/PR grants remain consumer-specific
and pending until the actual retained gates and current selected PR/head/evidence are observed.
An adopted/current merge policy may explicitly disclose automatic tag/build pipeline consequences
of its permitted merge. Those disclosed CI consequences belong to that merge scope; they grant no
separate manual tag/release action, workflow dispatch, production deployment, protection bypass,
real-data migration or secret rotation.

Retain private/pending ledger work, evidence refs and resource intents. Ordinary non-forced cleanup
may remove only clean owned audit roles after their outcomes/evidence are retained, published or
safely superseded. Keep refs when ordinary deletion refuses after squash; no force/prune/reset or
unrelated index/worktree cleanup follows. Development key/row verification must journal exact owned
scope before creation and reconcile cleanup before retry/completion; journal strings execute nothing.
These audit rules do not import maintenance report-push permission or triage's confined proof boundary.

A permitted audit-ledger update may use a separately recorded clean detached assessment worktree
at the freshly fetched default commit when shared main is dirty. This is part of the owned audit-ledger
role: record owner/path/base, keep assessment output private, and apply only in the separate owned
ledger branch after all audit gates. It grants no mutation or cleanup of unrelated worktrees.

# Loop settings

The optional `.vh-adlc/loop.yaml` is data, schema_version 1, written as block YAML.
`scripts/loop/settings.ts` reads it through the verified `vh-adlc` binary, with the file rules in
`triage-settings.md`: a settings file under another suffix fails and names `.vh-adlc/loop.yaml`. With
no settings file, every loop role keeps the host default and no binary is needed.

## Terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Loop role | One of `author`, `implementer`, `spec_reviewer` and `implementation_reviewer`; each has a route. |
| Route | How a role runs: `host` (in the current harness, optionally with a named model) or `command` (an external CLI, reviewer roles only). |
| Enrolled spec | A spec whose Review Log uses the shared header; a consumer's adapted commands send it to the vh-adlc operations. |
| Verification rung | A declared check with a path condition or `always`, which must pass before push, completion and delivery. |
| Project procedure | The consumer's file of local rules that every SDD operation reads, named by `project_procedure`. |
| Primary worktree | The first entry of `git worktree list`; with `implement_worktree: isolated`, implement never writes there. |
| No publication path | The delivery verdict for a merge commit that carries the skip marker and touches only skip-eligible paths. |
| Delivered | A feature whose release paths have all published, or whose merge has no publication path. |

## Roles

| Loop role | Operations |
| --- | --- |
| `author` | spec authoring, tasks, investigate |
| `implementer` | implement, ship |
| `spec_reviewer` | spec review |
| `implementation_reviewer` | implementation review |

Resume takes the route of the operation it continues.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | Required integer `1` when the file exists. |
| `roles.<role>.route` | `host` or `command`. A role that is not listed uses `host` with no model. |
| `roles.<role>.model` | Optional for `host`, passed to the host as a requested model under `review-protocol.md`. Required for `command`. |
| `roles.<role>.argv` | `command` only: the executable, then its arguments. It must contain `{prompt}` or `{prompt_file}`, and may use `{model}` and `{export_dir}`. No other placeholder is accepted. |
| `roles.<role>.model_attestation` | Optional, `command` only: `codex-session` reads the served model from Codex's session log for the run's thread id instead of the reviewer's self-report; the `argv` must include `--json`. A missing log, no or several recorded models, or a mismatch leaves the review pending. |
| `review_scratch` | Optional list of directories inside the checkout left out of the before-and-after check: build output a shell-enabled implementation reviewer may write to, and ignored directories other sessions or tools write while a review runs, such as other worktrees, temp roots and `node_modules`. Changes there do not leave the review pending. Never `.`. |
| `project_procedure` | Optional contained file of local rules. Every SDD operation reads it before acting. |
| `instruction_files` | Optional contained files, such as `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. Every SDD operation reads them, and every spec review checks the document against them. |
| `lenses` | Optional list of `{name, check, severity}`: a named check every spec review applies, with severity `blocking`, `should-fix` or `nit`. |

| `verification_rungs[].command` | A shell command run from the worktree. Exit 0 passes; exit 126 or 127 means it could not run; any other exit fails. |
| `verification_rungs[].procedure` | Instead of a command: a written procedure the operation performs and records. |
| `verification_rungs[].skipped_pattern` | Optional regular expression for an output line that reports a skipped mandatory subcheck; its first group names the subcheck. |

subcheck, blocks unless the owner allows that exact rung (`<rung>`) or subcheck (`<rung>/<subcheck>`) for
that run, and the report records the allowance. With rungs or a post-merge watch declared, a feature

content.content:
---
title: "Feature documents"
type: standard
description: "One living document per feature that is both its specification and its plan, with machine-checked rules."
status: active
---

# Feature documents

A feature is one observable outcome with accepted scope and verifiable criteria. Each feature has one
document that is both its specification and its plan. Do not create a companion spec, plan or notes file
for the same feature.

Enforcement: the `vh-adlc` binary reads the [rules block](#rules) at the repository's pinned revision of
this page and decides every status change with `vh-adlc gate`. Until that binary is released, these rules
are checked by hand, and a report says so.

## Location

A repository declares its feature root with one line in its root `AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
Feature documents: docs/specs/
```

Without that line, documents live in `docs/internal/plans/<slug>.md`. Do not move existing documents to
reach a default. A repository that keeps its own document format declares
`Feature document format: local` instead; this standard and its tooling then do not apply there.

## Frontmatter

```yaml
---
status: draft
status_description: "One line on the current state and what it waits for."
issue: https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/42
goal: "One observable outcome."
covers:
  - path/to/implementation/
---
```

`issue: null` marks local-only work; never invent a link. `covers` lists every path whose change can
affect the feature; the document itself is never covered. A document gains `branch` when implementation
starts and keeps it until the feature is closed.

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| draft | Being specified or revised | Authoring, or a normative revision |
| planned | Accepted by the owner and ready to build | The spec review step, after acceptance |
| in-progress | Being implemented on its feature branch | Implementation, as its first commit |
| complete | Every criterion met or residualised, reviewed | Implementation or shipping |
| blocked | Waiting on a named owner decision or external fix | Any step, naming the blocker |
| parked | Deliberately paused | The owner |
| abandoned | Will not be built | The owner |
| superseded | Replaced by another feature, which it links | The owner |
| archived | Closed history | The owner |

`complete` is terminal for its scope; new scope is a new feature. A blocked feature names the smallest
decision that clears it.

## Sections

Required, in this order: Context, Scope, Design, Acceptance Criteria, Test Plan, Tasks, Open Questions and
Review Log. Implementation Phases (before Tasks) and Sources (last) are optional. Delete a section that does
not apply rather than leave it empty, except the required ones, which may say "None.".

Scope, Design, Acceptance Criteria, Test Plan and the `covers` frontmatter form the normative baseline. A
change to any of them is a revision. Before the change is applied, a `planned` or `in-progress` document
moves to `draft` (on its feature branch when it has one); earlier reviews become stale, the owner accepts
again, and the document moves `draft` to `planned` before implementation re-enters through its branch.

Context and Design cite their claims: a `file:line`, or a command and its output, gathered when the claim
was written. Sources lists every external page read, each with the claim it supports.

### Owner summary in Context

New documents and documents undergoing a normative revision start Context with `### Owner summary`.
Use a few short paragraphs to explain the problem and outcome, scope, approach, important defaults,
permissions, trade-offs, validation state and owner decisions. Include migration or recovery where it
matters. Usually 250 to 400 words is enough; a small feature can be shorter. This is guidance for a
readable explanation, not a word-count gate.

The detailed normative sections remain authoritative. The summary must agree with them and distinguish
planned checks from observed proof. Refresh it when scope, proof or decisions change and before asking
for acceptance. Explain material changes since the last accepted scope. The reviewer checks for
contradictions, consequential omissions and unsupported claims through the existing finding records.
Keep the owner-facing conversation summary before acceptance as well.

Historical documents remain valid without this subsection. A summary-only prose correction does not
change the normative baseline or accept a feature. Keep stored review records verbatim; do not shorten
them to make the summary easier to find. The required top-level sections and machine-readable rules
below are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

```markdown
- [ ] AC-01: The end state, observable without reading the code.
```

State the end state, never a measurement of the problem. A criterion whose subject is a report, a count
or a warning can go green while the problem remains. IDs are never reused, and a failed criterion is
never deleted to make a result look complete.

A criterion is ticked only with evidence beneath it, or left unticked with a residual that names its
tracker:

```markdown
- [x] AC-01: The end state.
      Evidence: <command or action>, <target commit>, <observed result>, <limitations>
- [ ] AC-02: Another end state.
      Residual: https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/43
```

A residual needs the owner's decision. On a normative revision, every criterion tick, evidence line and residual
is reset; their history stays in Git and in the Review Log.

## Test plan

One table with exactly the header `| Criterion | Proof |`. Every criterion ID appears in its first column;
a cell may list several IDs separated by commas. Proof names a real check: a test, a scenario with a pass
condition, or a written manual procedure.

A proof that judges free text with a pattern lists its must-pass and must-fail examples in the row. A row
has passed review once a clean pass whose reviewed commit already held the row's current text has no
finding whose `WHERE` names that row or the Test Plan as a whole; a later change to the row starts over.
After that, a finding that only widens the pattern to catch more wrong output is a nit, and it is listed
rather than applied, even when the same pass changes the baseline for other findings. A finding that shows
the pattern rejects a correct output is blocking, because the proof then fails a correct implementation.

## Tasks

```markdown
- [ ] T1 `path/to/file_test.go` - the failing test for the new behaviour; fails because it does not exist (AC-01)
- [ ] T2 `path/to/file.go` - the change; T1 passes (AC-01)
```

One commit per task. Each names the file it touches, a done condition that is a test or check, and the
criteria it advances. Order by dependency, failing test first. Re-planning keeps checked tasks and changes
only the unchecked tail; new requirements get new task IDs.

## Open questions

Only the owner answers them. Write each for a decision in under a minute:

```markdown
### Q1: The question, as one plain sentence

**Recommendation:** A. The option, and one line on why.

| Option | You get | It costs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Name** | Benefit | Cost |
| **B. Name** | Benefit | Cost |

**Why this is yours:** what makes it a judgement call.
```

Every trade-off the document settles is an open question, including one the author would answer the same
way the owner would. A review finding rated nit is the exception: it follows the nit rule in
[Review log](#review-log) and is never raised as an open question. A section that weighs options and keeps
one, such as a simplification check, raises that choice here instead of deciding it. User-facing terms the
feature introduces or changes appear in a glossary row and are held to it by a criterion.

An answered question is folded into the document and removed. "None." means every question has been
answered, not that none was asked.

## Review log

One table row per review pass, then one `### R-<n>` subsection per pass holding the reviewer's returned
records verbatim:

```markdown
| Date | Review | Kind | Commit | Model | Isolation | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-17 | R-1 | spec | `0123abc` | <model that ran> | procedural | One line |
| 2026-10-17 | R-1 | spec | `0123abc` | n/a | n/a | accepted by owner |
```

`Kind` is `spec` or `implementation`. `Commit` is the exact reviewed commit; a `+dirty` suffix marks a
diagnostic review of uncommitted work, which never counts as current. `Isolation` is `structural` only
where the host enforces the reviewer's restrictions, otherwise `procedural` or `unknown`. A row with
`Outcome` exactly `accepted by owner` is an acceptance: it names the review it accepts, uses `n/a` for model
and isolation, and has no subsection.

A spec review returns complete finding records, or exactly `NO FINDINGS`:

```text
FINDING: F-01
KIND: factual | judgement
SEVERITY: blocking | should-fix | nit
WHERE: <section>
EVIDENCE: <file:line, command and output, or quote>
PROPOSAL: <one or two sentences>
```

Rate each finding by what it changes:

- blocking: a stated fact is false and that changes what is built, what a proof checks or how the
  binary reads the document; an implementer following the document would build something that does not
  solve the stated problem; a criterion cannot be met; or a proof fails a correct implementation or
  cannot be executed.
- should-fix: two careful implementers would build different things, or a proof could pass on a wrong
  implementation, except widening a free-text pattern row that has passed review to catch more wrong
  output, which is a nit (see [Test plan](#test-plan)).
- nit: wording, style, redundancy, or a citation slip that changes nothing an implementer builds or a
  proof checks. Widening a free-text pattern row that has passed review to catch more wrong output is also
  a nit.

A repository may declare review lenses, extra checks its reviews apply, each with its own severity. A
finding a declared lens raises takes that lens's severity; these definitions rate every other finding.

A nit on the normative baseline never causes a revision on its own. When the author applies a pass's
blocking or should-fix findings to the baseline, the same commit fixes every nit of that pass, in any
section and of either kind, without raising a judgement nit as an open question. The one exception is a
free-text widening nit, which stays listed even when the baseline changes for other findings. Every nit
the author does not apply, from every pass it handled in that invocation, is listed with its ID and one
line in its report and the owner-facing conversation summary, not in the document. A finding confined to
sections outside the normative baseline may be applied at any time, because it does not make the review
stale. A nit left unapplied stays in the document until a later revision touches it or the owner asks for
one.

Only the reviews that still decide something must be in record form: the latest spec review, the latest
implementation review, and the review the latest acceptance row names. Older subsections, including
earlier acceptances, are history.

An implementation review returns one record for every current criterion, with its exact accepted text:

```text
CRITERION: AC-01 <exact accepted text>
VERDICT: met | not met | untested | not verified
EVIDENCE: <command or action>, <target>, <observed result>, <limitations>
```

Criterion text is the text after `AC-NN: ` plus each following indented line, up to the next list item,
`Evidence:` line or `Residual:` line, with whitespace runs folded to one space and the ends trimmed. The record's text after
`CRITERION: AC-NN ` is folded the same way, and the two must be equal.

`met`: executed evidence observed in this review establishes the criterion. `not met`: executed evidence
contradicts it. `untested`: no adequate check covers it. `not verified`: a check exists but its execution
was not observed. A passing subset never upgrades a composite criterion.

## Acceptance

1. Fold the owner's answers into the document and commit. Call that commit X.
2. Run an independent spec review at X. Blocking findings are fixed and reviewed again by a new pass; a
   blocking pass is never relabelled clean.
3. The owner accepts in session.
4. Append the acceptance row naming that review.
5. Move the document to `planned` once the gate passes.

A request to investigate or draft is not permission to build, and an issue comment never changes a
status. A re-review caused only by changes on the default branch keeps the acceptance when the normative
baseline is unchanged.

## Rules

`vh-adlc` reads this block at the pinned revision. Exactly one block with this info string exists on this
page.

```yaml vh-adlc-rules
schema: 1
statuses: [draft, planned, in-progress, complete, blocked, parked, abandoned, superseded, archived]
transitions:
  draft: [planned, blocked, parked, abandoned, superseded]
  planned: [in-progress, draft, blocked, parked, abandoned, superseded]
  in-progress: [complete, draft, blocked, parked, abandoned, superseded]
  blocked: [draft, planned, in-progress, abandoned]
  parked: [draft, planned, abandoned]
  complete: [archived, superseded]
  superseded: [archived]
  abandoned: [archived]
feature_root:
  default: docs/internal/plans
  declaration: '^Feature documents: `?([^`\s]+)`?$'
required_frontmatter: [status, status_description, issue, goal, covers]
required_frontmatter_from: { in-progress: [branch] }
required_sections: [Context, Scope, Design, Acceptance Criteria, Test Plan, Tasks, Open Questions, Review Log]
normative_sections: [Scope, Design, Acceptance Criteria, Test Plan]
normative_frontmatter: [covers]
ids: { criterion: '^AC-\d{2,}$', task: '^T\d+$', review: '^R-\d+$' }
criterion_line: '^- \[( |x)\] (AC-\d{2,}):'
task_line: '^- \[( |x)\] (T\d+) '
evidence_line: '^\s+Evidence: '
residual_line: '^\s+Residual: (https://\S+|#\d+)'
open_question: '^### Q\d+: '
test_plan: { columns: [Criterion, Proof], criterion_cell: '^AC-\d{2,}(, AC-\d{2,})*$' }
review_log_columns: [Date, Review, Kind, Commit, Model, Isolation, Outcome]
review_commit: '^`?[0-9a-f]{7,40}(\+dirty)?`?$'
review_kinds: [spec, implementation]
isolation: [structural, procedural, unknown, n/a]
acceptance_row: { kind: spec, model: n/a, isolation: n/a, outcome: accepted by owner, subsection: false }
verdicts: [met, not met, untested, not verified]
record_criterion: '^CRITERION: (AC-\d{2,}) '
criterion_continuation: '^\s+\S'
record_verdict: '^VERDICT: (met|not met|untested|not verified)$'
record_finding: '^FINDING: F-\d{2,}$'
record_severity: '^SEVERITY: (blocking|should-fix|nit)$'
record_no_findings: '^NO FINDINGS$'
local_format_declaration: '^Feature document format: local$'
gates:
  planned: [no_open_questions, test_plan_complete, spec_review_fresh, spec_review_clean, accepted, on_feature_branch_if_set]
  in-progress: [no_open_questions, test_plan_complete, spec_review_fresh, spec_review_clean, accepted, tasks_populated, on_feature_branch_if_set]
  complete: [no_open_questions, test_plan_complete, spec_review_fresh, spec_review_clean, accepted, all_met, impl_review_fresh, impl_review_clean, feature_tree_clean, on_feature_branch_if_set]
next:
  - { status: [draft, planned, in-progress], when: not no_open_questions, do: owner decision }
  - { status: [draft, planned, in-progress], when: not on_feature_branch_if_set, do: owner decision }
  - { status: [draft, planned, in-progress], when: not test_plan_complete, do: spec }
  - { status: [draft, planned, in-progress], when: not spec_review_fresh, do: spec review }
  - { status: [draft, planned, in-progress], when: not spec_review_clean, do: spec }
  - { status: [draft, planned, in-progress], when: not accepted, do: owner acceptance }
  - { status: draft, do: spec }
  - { status: planned, when: not tasks_populated, do: tasks }
  - { status: planned, do: implement }
  - { status: in-progress, when: tasks_open, do: implement }
  - { status: in-progress, when: not feature_tree_clean, do: implement }
  - { status: in-progress, when: not impl_review_fresh, do: review }
  - { status: in-progress, when: not impl_review_clean, do: tasks }
  - { status: in-progress, when: not all_met, do: tasks }
  - { status: in-progress, do: ship }
  - { status: [blocked, parked], do: owner decision }
  - { status: [complete, abandoned, superseded, archived], do: none }
```

Every gate also checks the transition, except a gate whose target is the current status: that re-checks
the conditions only. The first matching `next` rule names the one next step. Lines in the block are
regular expressions where they start with `^`.

## Conditions

The block composes these conditions; `vh-adlc` implements them, and `vh-adlc fresh` decides staleness from
Git. A review bound to a changed normative baseline, a `+dirty` target, a missing review row or an
unreachable reviewed commit is stale.

| Condition | Holds when |
| --- | --- |
| `no_open_questions` | No line in Open Questions matches `open_question` |
| `test_plan_complete` | Every criterion ID appears in the Test Plan table |
| `spec_review_fresh` | The latest spec review exists and is not stale |
| `spec_review_clean` | The latest spec review is well formed and has no blocking finding, or is exactly `NO FINDINGS` |
| `accepted` | The latest acceptance row names a clean spec review whose commit has the current normative baseline |
| `tasks_populated` | At least one line matches `task_line` |
| `tasks_open` | At least one task is unticked |
| `on_feature_branch_if_set` | The document has no `branch`, or the current branch equals it |
| `all_met` | Every criterion is ticked with evidence, or unticked with a residual |
| `impl_review_fresh` | The latest implementation review exists and is not stale |
| `impl_review_clean` | That review has exactly one record per current criterion with its exact text, and each is `met` or residualised |
| `feature_tree_clean` | No staged, unstaged or untracked change matches `covers`, apart from the document itself |
---
title: "Feature document template"
type: guide
description: "Copy this template to start a feature document under the feature-document standard."
status: active
---

# Feature document template

Copy the block below into the repository's feature root, named `<slug>.md`. The
[feature-document standard](../conventions/feature-documents.md) defines every section and line format.
Replace each placeholder; never leave invented owners, dates, links or decisions behind.

````markdown
---
status: draft
status_description: "Being written; not yet reviewed."
issue: null
goal: "One observable outcome."
covers:
  - path/to/implementation/
---

# Plan: <Title>

<One or two sentences on what this delivers.>

## Context

### Owner summary

<Explain the outcome, included and excluded scope, proposed approach, consequential defaults,
permissions and trade-offs. Include migration or recovery when relevant. Distinguish planned checks
from observed proof; state review status, limitations and decisions needed. Explain what acceptance
authorizes. Use a few short paragraphs, usually 250 to 400 words, and less for a small feature.
Keep this explanation consistent with the detailed sections; they retain normative authority.>

### Background

<Why this is needed. Cite every claim about the current state with file:line, or a command and its output.>

## Scope

<What is in scope. Out of scope, by name: what someone might reasonably expect but will not get.>

## Design

<The design and its interfaces. Reference files and symbols; do not paste code.>

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-01: <The end state, observable without reading the code.>

## Test Plan

| Criterion | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| AC-01 | <The test, scenario or written manual procedure> |

## Tasks

None yet; written once the document is planned.

## Open Questions

### Q1: <The question, as one plain sentence>

**Recommendation:** A. <The option, and one line on why.>

| Option | You get | It costs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A. <Name>** | <Benefit> | <Cost> |
| **B. <Name>** | <Benefit> | <Cost> |

**Why this is yours:** <What makes it a judgement call.>

## Review Log

| Date | Review | Kind | Commit | Model | Isolation | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Sources

- [<Page title>](<exact URL>): <the claim it supports>
````
